description: We are a passionate team of young innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are looking for creative, enthusiastic, and dedicated members who are interested in space exploration, coding, designing, research, and problem-solving. Our goal is to collaborate, share ideas, learn new skills, and build something innovative together. No need to be an expert — curiosity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn are what matter most! 🌙
summary:
LunaMind is an interactive, NASA-powered educational lunar mission simulator developed to help students understand the challenges of living and working on the Moon. Inspired by the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, LunaMind allows users to experience a simulated seven-day lunar habitat mission while managing essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power.

The simulation includes mission events, crew management, objectives, and decision-making scenarios that demonstrate how choices can affect a lunar mission. It also integrates NASA's DONKI space weather data to introduce users to solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and geomagnetic storms. Historical radiation measurements from NASA RadLab are presented to help students explore the space radiation environment.

Built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Express.js, and Chart.js, LunaMind combines interactive learning with real NASA scientific data.

Our goal is to make space science engaging and accessible while inspiring the next generation of astronauts, engineers, and space researchers.
details:
LunaMind is an interactive educational lunar mission simulator designed to help students understand the challenges of living and working on the Moon. It creates a simulated seven-day lunar habitat mission in which users manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power while responding to mission events and making decisions that affect the mission.

The project includes a mission-control dashboard, resource monitoring, crew information, mission objectives, interactive events, and a space-weather section. It integrates NASA's DONKI data to introduce real space-weather events such as solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and geomagnetic storms. It also uses historical radiation measurements from NASA RadLab, including ISS DosTel data, to help users explore radiation measurements. These are historical ISS observations, not live lunar radiation measurements. The habitat resource levels and survival scenarios are simulated for educational purposes, not real spacecraft telemetry.

LunaMind was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Express.js, and Chart.js. Visual Studio Code was used for development, GitHub for source-code hosting, and Render for deployment.

The creative idea is to combine a space-themed interactive simulation with real NASA scientific resources. The project aims to make space science easier to explore, encourage critical thinking and decision-making, and inspire students to learn more about astronomy, engineering, and future lunar exploration.
